general.title: Welcome to Fellgorithm
general.d: Before you start, a few short cards on how Fellgorithm works, what’s important to know and how to make the best decisions for your own planning. Once you’ve read and agreed to each card, they join your relevant itineraries as a reminder. Your agreement stays only on this phone, with the date and time.

general.title: Pace Setting Considerations
general.t: Your pace setting is yours to get right.
general.d: Setting the right pace is one of the most important parts of your planning. Start with a short walk, at a pace you feel is generous to the slowest person in your group, then nudge the slider a little after each walk until it feels accurate. Fell running? The same applies: tiredness builds on long days, so be conservative, and remember to switch back for walks. Pace has its own section in the main settings, top left.

general.title: All Timings Are Estimates
general.d: Our timings are estimates, not guarantees. Every leg is worked out on real paths, with extra time for climbing, descents and rough ground. Routes assume clear, well-used paths between points and carry an extra {LEEWAY}% leeway. Weather conditions, the ground, your fitness and your group can still make a walk take much longer than planned. Your pace setting changes every timing, so keep it honest.

general.title: Finishing Before Sunset
general.t: Finishing before sunset is planned, not guaranteed.
general.d: Every route aims to get you off the fells {DARK} minutes before sunset but this is not guaranteed. Days slip, so always carry a head torch and turn back early using the reverse itinerary if you’re falling behind. A suggested kit list is on every itinerary, however it is your responsibility to make sure you and your group have everything needed for the route and the conditions on the day.

general.title: A Planning Aid Only
general.t: Fellgorithm is a planning aid, not a navigation or safety app.
general.d: Fellgorithm is a planning aid, not a navigation or safety app. It suggests an order of fells with start and finish points, as well as transport estimates. Fellgorithm never suggests a route is safe. Finding your way safely between the points on your itinerary is your responsibility. Walking in the mountains will always carry risk: pack a map and compass, know how to use them, and trust your own judgement on the route.

general.title: Check the Mountain Weather
general.t: Fellgorithm does not judge the weather.
general.d: By design, we never print the forecast on your itinerary. Mountain weather can change by the hour, so a forecast set in stone would soon be wrong. In poor conditions we may leave some routes out of our suggestions, but we never guarantee the conditions will suit a route we suggest. Cloud, wind and ice can make familiar ground hard to follow, so be ready to turn back early. Checking the mountain forecast before you go, and again on the day, is your responsibility.

general.title: Routes With a Bus Home
general.t: The bus home can never be guaranteed.
general.d: A red line (pictured) means the route relies on a bus home. It opens up many more routes, but adds risk. We never plan on the last bus — there are always at least {COVER} of later buses behind yours. Even so, buses can be late, cancelled, diverted or not run at all. Getting home if your bus doesn’t come is your responsibility, so always have a back-up plan. Want less risk? Switch off Routes that rely on a bus home in the main settings.

general.title: Routes With Splitter Buses
general.t: A splitter bus can never be guaranteed.
general.d: A yellow line (pictured) means the route includes a splitter bus: two walks joined by a bus in the middle of the day. This type of route carries the same risk as a bus home route, so it follows the same rules. Every itinerary includes a reverse itinerary to help reduce that risk, but a back-up plan in case your bus doesn’t arrive is your responsibility. The same switch in the main settings removes these routes from your planner.

general.title: Where Bus Times Come From
general.t: Bus times come from the official timetable data.
general.d: We only plan around buses in the operators’ published timetables, checked every day from the government’s Bus Open Data Service. These timetables can still be wrong or change at short notice, especially on bank holidays, so Fellgorithm can never guarantee the bus times on your itinerary. When a timetable changes, routes that relied on a missing bus drop out at the next daily check. Double checking that your buses are running on the day, at the times your route needs, is your responsibility.

general.title: Check Your Dates and Days
general.t: Routes are planned for the dates shown.
general.d: Seasonal routes rely on bus journeys that stop running, so they show an expiry date: a red leaf means a route has under {SOON} days left, amber means more. Every route is planned on your chosen day’s buses, which differ on weekdays, weekends and bank holidays. Always check the dates on your itinerary and never reuse an old one. Even the best-planned routes can change, so checking your bus times on the day is your responsibility.

general.title: Swirral Edge and Foxes Rake
general.t: Routes avoid Swirral Edge and Foxes Rake unless you switch that off.
general.d: By default, every itinerary avoids graded scrambles, with two exceptions left as an opt-in: Swirral Edge on Helvellyn and Foxes Rake on Scafell, because of the connections they make possible. You never need either to complete the 214 Wainwrights. Switching off Avoid Swirral Edge and Foxes Rake in the settings opens up quicker links in those areas, but adds risk: a slip can be fatal, especially in poor conditions. Your itinerary will say when a route uses one, and making sure everyone in your group is competent to take it on is your responsibility.

general.title: Multi Day Trip Considerations
general.t: Multi day trips are planned, not booked.
general.d: Multi day trips link up to seven days, from one basecamp, a different one each night, or a valley bus stop. Where you sleep is yours to arrange — wild camping in England needs the landowner’s permission. Every day keeps the same rules: off the fells before sunset, never the last bus, extra time for a heavier pack, and an escape bus at the end of each day or the start of the next. Buses can fail: a back-up plan for every day and night is your responsibility.

general.title: Before You Head Out
general.d: Tell someone your route and when you’ll be back. Charge your phone, but don’t count on signal in the fells. Pack your map, compass, head torch and the kit on your itinerary. In an emergency, call 999, ask for Police, then Mountain Rescue. Most of all — enjoy the fells.

avoidScr.title: Routes May Use Swirral Edge or Foxes Rake

items.t: Swirral Edge and Foxes Rake are graded scrambles.
items.d: Both are steep, exposed rock where a slip can be fatal, and much harder in wet, wind or ice. There may be no easy way off once you are on them.

items.t: Only take them on if you have the experience.
items.d: Fellgorithm names them on any itinerary that uses them, but cannot judge whether you, your group or the conditions are up to it.

items.t: Your planned bus home may leave little room for error.
items.d: With this off, a route can plan on a bus home with less than {COVER} of later buses after it. If you miss it, or it does not run, there may be no other bus home that day.

appRules.note: The app's safety rules in force. GENERATED from the app (APP_RULES in Fellgorithm.dc.html) — never edit by hand. Republished with every app release; the nightly audit quotes it and flags a HIGH problem if the released app's rules differ.
appRules.scrambles: Only Swirral Edge and Foxes Rake, and only with Avoid Swirral Edge and Foxes Rake switched off, and only when the way round is at least 45 minutes longer; every other graded scramble never
